strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy.stats.loglaplace moment divergence: on buggy commit e7d71d6d6827 _munp returns c**2/(c**2-n**2) unconditionally, giving a finite negative value for |n|>=c (e.g. mean at c=0.5 gives -0.3333). The developer test test_moments_stats in scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py asserts moment(r,c)==inf and that stats(c, moments=...) has no finite values; it should fail on buggy and pass once _munp returns inf (np.where on |n|<c) for divergent orders.

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy e7d71d6d6827 the parametrized test_moments_stats cases fail because loglaplace.moment(r, c) returns finite negative values instead of inf; on the fixed revision (condition changed so divergent orders return inf) all four parametrizations pass.

Boundary ambiguity: the two diff variants (n**2 < c**2 versus np.abs(n) < c) may differ at n == c; the developer test uses c = arange(0.5, r+0.5, 0.5) which includes c == r, so the fixed-side result at the boundary depends on which variant is in the fixed revision.

Numpy version is not evidenced; behaviour of c**2/(c**2-n**2) with n integer is stable across versions, but the chosen numpy version is an assumption.
Issue number and PR date are not stated in the evidence (PR DATE is blank), so the exact era of the buggy commit is inferred from the commit hash only.
